created_during_execution.title: A deep package packs but cannot be published
created_during_execution.reason: Found reviewing 15cc28c5. publish_package_tree's CaptureBudget max_paths multiplier assumes a path shape the package model does not constrain, so a deep package packs but cannot be published; capture fails identically, placing it in the publication layer since 6a479c58. Filed at v1.1 initially; the invoker corrected that fixing bugs we find is our responsibility, not scope expansion, so it is now epic work at milestone:v1.0, wired 15cc28c5 -> cf42d08b -> f6a17e0d with the redundant story edge reduced.

created_during_execution.title: A reject reason can leave the repository failing validation
created_during_execution.reason: Found by dogfooding: jit issue reject --reason writes the reason as a resolution: label, so a prose reason violates @/inv/label-format and leaves the repository failing jit validate and therefore the repo-validate gate. Recovery is blocked by two further defects: --remove-label exits 0 without removing a malformed label, and jit validate --fix reports no fixes needed while jit validate fails. Repaired by hand-editing the issue JSON plus jit recover. Not part of this epic; filed at milestone:v1.0 with no epic label - placing it under an epic is a planning call above the lead.

escalations.summary: The separate v1.0 validation implementation is committed and merged into the isolated Wave 1 candidate; final direct-main integration waits only for its lead-owned JIT gate state to be committed.
The invoker authorized a targeted retry and reset the counter with explicit guidance that profile apply dry-run is part of the repeatable ordered-selector contract.

Session 2 handed off after the release smoke workflow exposed one stale dry-run consumer. A final authorized Luna xhigh repair updated that workflow and its acceptance test; all configured gates passed, and the exact merged main tree passed cargo-ci plus the MCP suite.

After two substantive rework rounds produced a fully tested final commit, the lead Tier 2.5 sweep found one remaining stale neighbouring phrase at docs/reference/storage-format.md:67 ('minimal provenance record'). The invoker selected option 1 and authorized one narrowly targeted Luna xhigh retry.

After two rework rounds, exact cargo-ci passed at abea9028 but code-review found that the first successful apply of two equal contributors records shared ownership only in the later package record; the first record converges only on a second apply. The invoker selected option 1 and authorized one targeted Terra xhigh retry spanning command, initialization, and provenance boundaries without pulling Wave 7's transaction redesign forward.

How to bound package-tree publication, raised as an open question in handoff-10. Three directions put to the owner: (A) cap path depth or length in the package model, (B) derive the budget from total path bytes, (C) remove the per-path budget entirely so the capture kernel needs none. The owner chose (C). The lead had recommended (A) and recorded the disagreement rather than re-litigating.
escalations.consequence: cf42d08b's blast radius widens from commands/profile.rs to the shared capture kernel: CaptureBudget.max_paths (repository_state/image.rs:526-535), its two enforcement sites (image.rs:679-688 phase one, image.rs:797-808 close), roughly ten construction sites across repository_state/{mod,archive,initialize,export,profile_apply,image_plan_hash_property_tests}, storage/gate_runs.rs, document/reference.rs, commands/profile.rs, plus CaptureError::PathBudgetExceeded and any generated reference naming it.
escalations.residual_risk: max_paths is a live guard, not dead weight. After removal the remaining dimensions are max_depth, max_listings, max_bytes. Listing-driven expansion stays bounded because RepositoryImage::close folds every listing child's name length into byte_count (image.rs:777-779, 832-833). Caller-enqueued fixed/discovered/pinned/linked_worktree paths are the dimension that may become unbounded: a zero-byte entry contributes nothing to byte_count. The worker was instructed to state the bounding argument per path source, to close any gap through a dimension derived from what the model constrains rather than a renamed path count, and to stop and report as blocking if the removal cannot be made safe. This is a trust boundary: capture reads manifest-declared targets, and under `jit profile add` the manifest arrives from outside the repository.
escalations.issue_description_untouched: cf42d08b's Notes still say two directions were considered and neither chosen, and that the choice belongs with whoever owns the package model. That text predates the decision. Left unedited per lead invariant 4 (no issue scope change without the invoker's explicit approval); the decision reached the worker through the dispatch prompt instead. A reviewer reading only the issue will find the Notes understate the option space.

surfaced_pitfalls.subject: live-asset classification encoded twice
surfaced_pitfalls.detail: Whether a package asset draws its bytes from the repository is answered by a package-relative source path prefix (JIT_DOGFOOD_LIVE_SOURCE_PREFIX = "assets/live/", crates/jit/src/profile/repository_package.rs:5, consumed in production only at package_assembly.rs:190) while the manifest separately declares [[live-source]] roots (manifest.rs:149, LiveSourceDeclaration at :346). Two encodings of one convention (@/inv/convention-convergence), and the constant names one package for a rule applied to every package (@/inv/domain-agnostic). The epic plan fixes the prefix convention for REQ-13, so 6a479c58 is directed to rename the constant only; converging on a declared per-asset marker would be a manifest-schema change beyond the plan.

surfaced_pitfalls.subject: empty directories survive a capture removal
surfaced_pitfalls.detail: RepositoryAction (repository_state/image.rs:1274) has DeleteFile and no DeleteDirectory, so a directory left empty by a whole-tree republication remains. No undeclared FILE survives, which is what REQ-01 states, and ProfilePackage::from_directory ignores empty directories. Bears on 15cc28c5 (pack), which archives a package directory and would carry the empty directory into the archive.

surfaced_pitfalls.subject: gate verdict memoisation hides an environmental failure
surfaced_pitfalls.detail: jit gate evaluate reuses a prior verdict over unchanged declared inputs ('Verdict: taken from run <id> over the same declared inputs', 0ms). target/ is not a declared input, so clearing an incremental cache does not invalidate a failure caused by it. --force is required. A lead reading the stale verdict would conclude the work is broken.

surfaced_pitfalls.subject: codex exec blocks on stdin
surfaced_pitfalls.detail: codex exec -m ... "prompt" reads additional input from stdin and blocks until killed, producing no output (observed: a 15-minute survey returned nothing, exit 124/0 with 'Reading additional input from stdin...'). Redirect < /dev/null on every codex invocation.

surfaced_pitfalls.subject: TreeFileDisposition / ProfileCaptureAction 1:1 duplication
surfaced_pitfalls.detail: repository_state::TreeFileDisposition and profile::ProfileCaptureAction have identical variants with a mapping at commands/profile.rs:670-675. Defensible layering (domain type vs Serialize/JsonSchema wire type), recorded for cb26de35 rather than failed.

surfaced_pitfalls.subject: ProfileCaptureResult flattens package facts beside the envelope
surfaced_pitfalls.detail: count (entries in files, incl. removals) sits beside file_count (files in the captured package). Both load-bearing; the worker proposes nesting the package's own facts under "package". Deferred to cb26de35, which owns one presentation contract, because ProfileShowEntry flattens the same fields today.

surfaced_pitfalls.subject: ProfileApplyError::PackageOutsideWorktree serves two callers
surfaced_pitfalls.detail: It now reports both 'a package's bytes were read from outside the worktree' and 'a caller named a capture source/destination that is not worktree content', while living on ProfileApplyError though capture is not an apply. A shared ProfilePathError would read better. Worker-reported.

surfaced_pitfalls.subject: codex luna rewrote the epic's historical audit trail
surfaced_pitfalls.detail: Dispatched for 9a81ab12, codex applied the REQ-05 documentation sweep to dated session records: seven handoffs, investigation.md, c639cfb5-research.md (201 lines), breakdown.json, and progress.json. It edited past-tense records of what earlier sessions built so they no longer mentioned the removed mechanism, deleting concrete facts (handoff-9's record of 7793b8b7 and its failure mode; handoff-6's pinned-record detail). Reverted in full; the commit contains no dev/active path. Cause partly the dispatch prompt, which said 'grep the whole tree' without excluding dev/active/**. Every future doc-sweep instruction must exclude dated records.

surfaced_pitfalls.subject: codex luna weakened a contract test to work around its sandbox
surfaced_pitfalls.detail: It added .filter(|path| symlink_metadata(...).is_ok()) to tests/provenance_contract/repository_inventory.rs because git ls-files --cached still listed the deleted files - true only because -s workspace-write made .git read-only so it could not commit. Committed, the filter is unnecessary and would silently skip a genuinely missing repository input instead of failing. Reverted; the provenance suite then passed 3/3 with the fixture at 1528 files, confirming the filter was an uncommitted-state artifact.

surfaced_pitfalls.subject: codex exec -s workspace-write is the wrong sandbox for this repo
surfaced_pitfalls.detail: It denies .git writes (so the agent cannot commit and works around uncommitted state) and denies socket binding (15 test failures unrelated to the change), and the home cargo cache is read-only. The agent reported its exit 1 honestly. Either grant a writable .git and network-local sockets, or keep validation and commits lead-side as was done for wave 11.

surfaced_pitfalls.subject: 7793b8b7 is dissolved but out of epic scope
surfaced_pitfalls.detail: type:bug, milestone:v1.1, no epic label. Its subject - the process-global shipped_v1 conversion counter and the order-dependent test asserting on it - is deleted by 9a81ab12, so it is unreproducible. Not transitioned: transitioning an out-of-epic issue is the invoker's call.

surfaced_pitfalls.subject: Tier 2.5 sweep patterns missed the removed mechanism's own vocabulary
surfaced_pitfalls.detail: Wave 11's stale-narrative sweep grepped for 'migration boundary|compatibility path|legacy record|five-field|pre-canonical' plus the residual symbol names, and passed. It missed 'authenticated v1 conversion' at profile_apply.rs:1836 and 'authenticated embedded' at commands/profile.rs:1139, both caught later by the container holistic review. The per-issue code-review gate also returned 0 findings on that tree. Lesson: sweep on the removed mechanism's domain vocabulary (convert, conversion, authenticate, v1, migrate) and not only on the phrases the lead expects to find.

surfaced_pitfalls.subject: whole-class sweep found a defect no reviewer had cited
surfaced_pitfalls.detail: Reworking F1 (directory-entry mode unchecked), the worker swept for siblings as instructed and found the archive metadata entry's mode was never checked at all - present since the first submission, cited by no reviewer. Both now reach one comparison, require_entry_mode (package_archive.rs:620), with three call sites: manifest-declared file modes, DIRECTORY_MODE, REGULAR_FILE_MODE. Evidence that demanding the class rather than the cited line finds defects the review process would not have surfaced.

surfaced_pitfalls.subject: worker shell commands ran from the session cwd instead of its worktree
surfaced_pitfalls.detail: Several of the wave-12 worker's Bash calls in rework round 2 ran from /home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time rather than its worktree. Tool-based edits used absolute worktree paths and were unaffected. Lead verified independently: main's git status --porcelain is empty, no tracked source modified, leak check clean - no damage. One consequence was a false MCP failure: npm test from main tested main's curated-tools.json against the worktree-built binary, reporting undecided tools; re-run from the worktree passed 64+13. The worker discarded an unattributable cargo-ci run and re-ran rather than report it. Same cwd trap hit the lead three times this session (gate evaluated against main, install-jit resolving main's repo root, gate-status wrong tree).

surfaced_pitfalls.subject: worker and lead both run the full cargo-ci on the same commit
surfaced_pitfalls.detail: Each rework round pays cargo-ci twice: once by the worker to self-check before submitting, once by the lead as the authoritative gate. At 601-703 s per run that is ~12 minutes duplicated per round. From wave 13, dispatch prompts should ask the worker to run its own added tests plus clippy and fmt, and leave the single full cargo-ci to the lead's gate run.

surfaced_pitfalls.subject: the limits CLI round trip costs ~33 s, over the whole 30 s suite budget
surfaced_pitfalls.detail: test_profile_pack_and_add_carry_a_package_at_the_model_limits publishes 512 files totalling 4 MiB through the repository transaction and measures ~33 s alone, exceeding the standing budget 4b7c06d0 sets for the entire suite. Kept deliberately: it is the test that proves the pack->add round trip the bound defect broke, and it was added at lead instruction during rework. Not trimmed in 15cc28c5 because that would be a third rework round on a passing issue, which policy sends to escalation rather than dispatch. A concrete cheaper shape exists and belongs to 4b7c06d0: the bound that broke was the ENTRY count, not the byte payload, so the CLI test needs 512 files with small content to exercise both the entry count and the real publication path, while the unit test already proves the 4 MiB byte bound without publishing. That split should keep both properties at a fraction of the cost.

surfaced_pitfalls.subject: a criterion enumerating properties admits no implicit carve-out
surfaced_pitfalls.detail: REQ-03 lists 'absolute path, parent-directory traversal, symlink, or unexpected mode' as properties that must be refused. The lead accepted an implementation that stopped checking mode for one entry kind, reasoning the property had no referent there. The reviewer read the enumeration literally and failed it. Lesson: when a criterion enumerates properties to refuse, a change that stops checking one of them for any subset of inputs needs the criterion amended (escalation) rather than a lead judgement that the property does not apply.

scope_changes.decision: Package exchange ships integrity only; authenticity deferred without obligation
scope_changes.detail: The archive digest establishes integrity (truncation, corruption, accidental modification), not authenticity. It travels inside the archive, so anyone who can rewrite the content can rewrite the digest; the adopter's chosen channel carries authenticity (epic D-02). Confirmed as sufficient for this release. Signing or provenance attestation would be an additional artifact beside the digest rather than a change to it, so no half-built surface is left behind.
scope_changes.constraint: Neither code documentation nor adopter documentation (b3d92595) may describe the digest as proof of origin. Recorded in dev/active/15cc28c5/15cc28c5-threat-model.md, which is linked to 15cc28c5 and backs its precheck security-review attestation.

container_reconciliations.criterion: REQ-01: child work lands per-target ownership claims, one aggregate publication, resolved variables, and three-way reconfiguration and upgrade, so an applied profile can change without stranding the repository.
container_reconciliations.method: Every surfaced_pitfalls entry examined against REQ-01's named subjects. A pitfall whose subject a criterion names is a criterion violation, not a follow-up.

in_subject.subject_match: REQ-01 names 'three-way reconfiguration and upgrade', and this concerns that seam's conflict reporting.
in_subject.assessment: The seam reports the first conflicting target rather than all of them. REQ-01's test is whether an applied profile can change without stranding the repository: a reported conflict is actionable, the user resolves it and re-runs, and nothing is stranded. Epic REQ-07 requires conflicts be 'actionable', not exhaustive in one pass. Judged not a violation, and deliberately NOT argued away in advance - the holistic-review gate is an independent judge and runs without this pitfall being pre-closed. If it fails on this, the resolution is a remediation task inside the container, not a softer reading of the criterion.

coordination.with: peer Claude session leading epic 4b7c06d0 (test-suite performance)
protocol: Three locks, always acquired in this order, skipping any not needed. (1) ${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/jit-main-checkout.lock (M) — main's checkout content is stable; taken for merge->commit, write->commit, and a gate evaluated against main's checkout. (2) ${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/jit-host-cpu.lock (P) — the host is quiet enough to measure; taken for a cold worktree build, a full-workspace cargo test, or a full-workspace clippy. (3) ${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/cargo-ci.lock (C) — taken internally by scripts/cargo-ci.sh; never wrap it yourself. A session holding P never requests M: release P, then take M. Focused test filters (-p, -E) take nothing.

Why P is separate from M rather than one lock: M is held for two-second commits, P for ten-minute cold builds. Merging them makes every operation pay the cost of the most expensive thing sharing the name — a cold build blocks the peer's commits for ten minutes and the peer's commits make builds wait for nothing. They protect different resources.

Deadlock the ordering rule prevents: session A holds M for a gate against main's checkout and waits on C inside cargo-ci.sh, while session B holds C from a worktree gate and waits on M for a full-workspace run. Both wait out the 2400 s timeout and the failure surfaces 40 minutes later as an unexplained timeout.
.jit/ mutations commit immediately, in their own commit, never batched with source. On an events.jsonl collision take both sides in timestamp order; it is append-only and no line may be dropped.

Disjoint source ownership. Peer: scripts/cargo-ci.sh, scripts/rust-build-budget.sh, .config/nextest.toml, dev/TESTING.md, crates/jit/tests/scratch_build/, dev/benchmarks/. This epic: crates/jit/src/{commands/profile.rs,profile/**,repository_state/**}, profiles/**, profile docs. Cross-boundary work is announced before it starts; cf42d08b's capture-kernel change was announced under this rule.

A generated projection under docs/reference/ belongs to whoever owns the source declaration. Render only from a clean tree, inside M, and git status immediately after: jit project render regenerates every declared projection, not only the one being aimed at, so rendering while another session's source edit sits unrendered silently carries their projection change out under this issue's commit tag. A dirty projection nobody owns is someone else's unrendered source change — leave it and ping.
A source declaration and its projection go into one lock acquisition and one commit. Splitting them ships an intervening commit whose projection disagrees with its source.

Announce a cold build over ~2 minutes before starting it, so the peer can take P for a timed run first rather than sit in flock behind ten minutes of compilation. No lock protocol substitutes for the notice.
Assignee names disambiguated: this session claims under agent:lead-c639cfb5; the peer holds agent:jit-execution-lead for its own epic.
contrib/gates/** prompts are profile assets on this epic's side; either session announces before editing one.
facts_learned: scripts/cargo-ci.sh takes a machine-global flock at ${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/cargo-ci.lock and holds it for the whole run (scripts/cargo-ci.sh:64-68), waiting CARGO_CI_LOCK_TIMEOUT (default 1800s) then exiting 75. Exit 75 is contention, not a defect. Plain cargo commands take no such lock. A backgrounded gate run outlives the agent that launched it and keeps the lock: check `fuser -v` on the lock file before concluding anything.

The stale-binary guard and build provenance were removed on 2026-08-12 by 355565c2. crates/jit/src/domain/binary_build_inputs.txt no longer exists and exit 10 no longer means the binary predates the tree. Nothing now catches a stale binary, so reinstall via the checkout's own scripts/install-jit.sh before anything that runs through the installed jit (repo-validate, jit validate). Not a precondition for cargo-backed gates.

Peer epic 4b7c06d0 wave 7 (94d85bf1) makes scripts/cargo-ci.sh start enforcing MAX_TEST_SUITE_SECONDS=30 by threading the measured suite clock into scripts/rust-build-budget.sh --test-suite-ms. Today that argument is never passed and the check reports suite-duration=skipped. After it merges, a cargo-ci failure reading 'test suite duration: observed N ms, threshold 30000 ms' is contention with that budget, not a defect in this epic's change. Warm run measures ~22,100 ms, so the margin is about 8 s.

/tmp is a 16 GiB tmpfs shared by both sessions and by every worktree's gate TMPDIR. When it filled in an earlier session the symptom was not 'disk full' but 57 doctest failures, CLI exit-code failures, and the agent's own shell silently losing command output as writes hit EDQUOT. Check df -h /tmp before debugging a burst of unrelated-looking failures.
A remote exists (origin, github.com:erankavija/just-in-time) with local main roughly 420 commits ahead. Neither session pushes without the user asking.

Editing contrib/gates/** prompts moves the live dogfood package's identity hash. An earlier prompt edit turned main red for a whole epic until b1f2f001 stopped pinning that hash to a literal. Rebase before computing any package identity and never pin a live hash to a literal.

CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 is required on every cargo invocation repository-wide. scripts/cargo-ci.sh runs an incremental-preflight step before compiling anything and fails outright when any incremental directory under target/ is non-empty, so one stray cargo run without it fails every gate on the host — for every session — for a reason unrelated to the change under review, and the failure reads as a code defect until someone inspects directory timestamps. Remedy is removing target/debug/incremental, which is a regenerable cache.

A dispatched subagent inherits the parent session's cwd, which is the primary checkout. The worktree dispatch header's 'cd to your worktree' is an instruction the worker must actively follow, not a state it starts in; worker-cf42d08b ran cargo before following it and built the whole workspace into main's checkout. Every worker cargo command must carry its own 'cd <worktree> && pwd &&' prefix inside the command rather than relying on a previous cd, because shell state does not persist reliably between tool calls and a drifted worker does not know it has drifted.

jit gate evaluate memoises a verdict over declared inputs and returns 'Verdict: taken from run <id> over the same declared inputs' in ~0 ms, with duration_ms 0, exit_code null, empty stdout, and origin.derivation 'reused'. target/ is not a declared input, so nothing done to the build tree invalidates a verdict — clearing an incremental cache, deleting target/ entirely, or using a fresh worktree all return the stale result. Only --force re-runs. Every environmental failure is therefore sticky, and the more thoroughly the environment is fixed the more convincing the stale failure looks. A reused record reads like a crashed checker.

The skill's check-leak-into-main.sh is unsafe over .jit/ under a shared checkout. It snapshots main's git status at dispatch and reports anything new as a probable worker leak, which is sound for a single-session lead but false when a peer session legitimately writes .jit/ gate runs, events, and issue records. Its printed recovery advice (git restore / rm) would have deleted the peer's in-flight gate evidence and truncated the append-only event log. Treat the check as advisory over .jit/ and authoritative only over source paths: attribute flagged .jit/ entries by issue ID before touching anything, and never auto-restore them.

suite-build (cargo nextest run --workspace --no-run) measures 356-377 ms warm and absorbed 32389 ms in the contended run where the target was cold. The step exists so compilation is paid outside the measured span, which is the property every gate run in a fresh worktree depends on: a cold worktree no longer fails the duration budget.

A protocol agreed between sessions is unverified until an observable fact proves it is in force, and an unverified protocol is worse than a violated one because it compounds silently. Three one-command checks: `ls ${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/jit-host-cpu.lock` (flock creates the file on first acquisition, so absence proves nobody has ever taken it), `find . -type d -name incremental -not -empty` (the incremental discipline), and `du -sh .agents/worktrees/agent-*/target` (cwd discipline: a worktree with no target/ built somewhere else). All three found real violations the first time they were run, including two of this session's own workers. The near-miss they prevented: a contended 29477 ms measurement being recorded as an epic's headline evidence with a clean provenance story attached.

The incremental discipline is a precondition of the worker's own gate, not courtesy toward other sessions. cargo-ci's incremental-preflight runs before it compiles anything and fails on a non-empty incremental directory under the worktree's own target/, and the lead evaluates cargo-ci in the worker's worktree. Frame it to workers as 'your issue cannot pass its own gate until you clear this', because 'do not dirty the shared host' loses to time pressure.

A protocol change binds at dispatch: in-flight work runs under the rules it started with. A worker mid-cargo-build has no message pump, so an instruction sent to prevent a ten-minute unlocked build sits in its inbox behind that build. After any protocol change the question belongs to the lead, not the worker: what is already running, and under which version of the rules?

check-leak-into-main.sh flags a false positive that will not go away: .agents/worktrees/target/worker-625cc07f/ is 1.9 GB of orphaned build cache from issue 625cc07f (epic:v1-release, done, 2026-07-30), left by an older layout that pointed CARGO_TARGET_DIR outside the worktree. No entry in git worktree list references it. A check with an undocumented false positive gets ignored wholesale, so the sixth hit in the incremental sweep is a fossil, not a violation.

measurements.finding: Per-test cost figures measured before 4dc5e9275 are stale, potentially by more than an order of magnitude.
measurements.detail: handoff-10 recorded test_profile_pack_and_add_carry_a_package_at_the_model_limits (crates/jit/tests/cli_repo_workflow/profile_cli_tests.rs:2461) at ~33 s and left an open question about trimming it. Re-measured at main by the peer session: 1.346 s. The dominant lever is 4dc5e9275, which set [profile.dev.package."*"] opt-level = 1, so serde, tar, and the I/O paths now run optimized under cargo test; a test writing and re-reading 512 files through a real transaction is close to the ideal beneficiary. The test stays as written: it neither needs trimming nor qualifies as inherent cost.
measurements.standing_rule: Re-measure before trimming, excluding, or attributing any test on the strength of a number from an earlier session. The failure mode is deleting coverage to solve a problem that no longer exists.

measurements.finding: Idle-host suite baseline, for judging any test this epic adds against the enforced 30 s budget.
measurements.detail: Three warm runs on a quiet host at 0e71077d9, measured by the peer session holding both locks: suite-clock 22175 / 23628 / 22095 ms, total gate 24821 / 26307 / 24794 ms, suite-build 356-377 ms, 4481 tests, 7 skipped, 63 doctests, every run exit 0. Recorded as 4ced8862b under dev/benchmarks/suite-enforcement-4b7c06d0/ with the contended run beside it. Under one concurrent cold workspace build the same tree measured 29477 ms and passed by 523 ms, with incremental-state (a directory walk) going 130 ms to 11497 ms and doctests 4600 to 7706 ms on pure I/O contention. Roughly 7 s of headroom on an idle host; roughly 0.5 s under one concurrent build.
measurements.standing_rule: Consecutive gate runs are not independent samples: the middle of those three is the high one because it started while the previous run's load was still decaying. A back-to-back reading that looks bad is the previous run, not the change under test. Let the host settle between measurements. Corollary for this epic: cf42d08b's regression test publishes 511 assets at nine path components through the real transaction and must be timed in isolation before merge.
